2026-10-01.headline: Mercury sextile Lilith
2026-10-01.text:
October 1, 2026 — a note from the sky, and from the data.

Today: Mercury sextile Lilith.

Between 1974 and 2005 this appeared on 318 trading days. Over the next trading day, the seasonally-adjusted return of a broad 52-instrument composite ran −0.08 percentage points below the rest of the sample (z = -2.54, p = 0.011).

Read in isolation, that looks like something. It is not. It is one of 752 sky configurations tested across the full record, and none survived correction for multiple testing. Out of sample (2006–2026) the pattern did not hold.

A later re-run that fixed a missing-aspect bug widened the search to 932 configurations. It still found none that beat chance.

This is what a false positive looks like in financial data: a clean number that dissolves the moment it is measured against the whole search.

The full falsification test — 52 years, 13,725 trading days, ~180,996 observations — is published in the open, methods and code included.

Read the study → https://astrotraderpro.com

Between 1974 and 2005 this appeared on 267 trading days. Over the next trading day, the seasonally-adjusted return of a broad 52-instrument composite ran +0.08 percentage points above the rest of the sample (z = 2.44, p = 0.015).

A later re-run that fixed a missing-aspect bug widened the search to 932 configurations. It still found none that beat chance.

This is what a false positive looks like in financial data: a clean number that dissolves the moment it is measured against the whole search.
